data.reasoning: Both models successfully audited the executable files (PKGBUILD and gen.sh) and found no malicious behavior. The package simply downloads pre-built GRUB themes from the official GitHub repository and installs them. The disagreement was solely due to an API error (HTTP 400) in the qwen model when processing the .SRCINFO metadata file, which does not represent a security risk.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool failure (HTTP 400 API error) in the qwen model when reviewing .SRCINFO, forcing an 'inconclusive' verdict. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and found them safe. There was no substantive security disagreement.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review .SRCINFO due to an API error (HTTP 400).
learnings: Tool errors (e.g., API timeouts or 400 errors) on non-executable metadata files like .SRCINFO should not override a 'safe' verdict if the actual build scripts (PKGBUILD, .install) have been successfully audited and cleared.
The audit tool should distinguish between 'inconclusive due to security ambiguity' and 'inconclusive due to tool failure', perhaps allowing a fallback verdict if critical files are safe.
